summary: Describes a framework and scenarios for dual-homing protection of pseudowires, which avoids unnecessary switchovers and does not depend on a control plane. A special pseudowire between the two edge nodes carries traffic when a failure occurs. It is informational.

eli5.summary: If the front door of a house is blocked, a hallway between two doors lets you reach the other. This explains how that works in networks.

questions: how do dual-homed pseudowires fail over
subtitle: A spare pseudowire between two edge routers keeps a failure on one side from forcing changes on the other.

tldr.problem: When a link or router fails in a dual-homed pseudowire setup, switching everything over can cause massive switchovers and congestion, and existing redundancy mechanisms depend on a dynamic control plane.
tldr.mechanism: A Dual-Node Interconnection pseudowire (DNI-PW) between the two dual-homing PE nodes carries traffic so that a failure on the attachment circuit side or the network side is handled locally.
tldr.outcome: The framework works with or without a control plane and complements existing protection mechanisms. The coordination protocol itself is in RFC 8185.

today: RFC 8184 is an Informational RFC that has not been obsoleted or updated by a later RFC. The coordination mechanism it relies on is defined in the companion RFC 8185.

sections.title: Why Dual-Homing Protection
sections.content:
MPLS-TP linear protection (RFC 6372, RFC 6378) protects the path between edge nodes, but not against failure of the attachment circuit (AC) or the provider edge (PE) node. Pseudowire redundancy (RFC 6718, RFC 6870) does, but it relies on LDP signaling, so it needs a dynamic control plane. RFC 8104 is also limited to dynamic control planes.

In mobile backhauling, a customer edge (CE) node on one side may be dual-homed to two PEs. If the primary AC fails, operators prefer to switch only on the dual-homing side and keep the working pseudowires. This avoids massive PW switchover in the mobile core site and congestion from moving traffic off the paths network planners prefer. Likewise, when one working PW fails, it is preferable to keep the working AC.
sections.eli5: If one road breaks, you want only the nearby traffic to take a detour, not everyone in the whole city.

sections.title: The Dual-Homing PE Architecture
sections.content:
The PE architecture builds on Figure 4a of RFC 3985. Besides the AC and the service PW toward the remote PE, a DNI-PW connects the forwarders of the two dual-homing PEs. It carries traffic between them when a failure occurs on the AC side or the service PW side.

RFC 3985 makes switching the job of the forwarder. Here the forwarder switches payloads among three entities: the AC, the service PW and the DNI-PW.
sections.eli5: The DNI-PW is the hallway between the two doors. The doorkeeper decides whether to send you to the street, the other door, or the hallway.

sections.title: One-Side Dual-Homing
sections.content:
In the one-side scenario, CE1 is dual-homed to PE1 and PE2 while CE2 is single-homed to PE3. AC1 is active, AC2 is standby, PW1 is working and PW2 is the protection PW. This can protect against failure of PE1 or PE2, an AC failure, and a PSN failure affecting the working PW. The text suggests mobile backhaul, with CE2 as a cell site such as a NodeB and CE1 as the shared Radio Network Controller.

  • AC1 fails: AC2 becomes active, PE2 connects AC2 to the DNI-PW, and PE1 connects the DNI-PW to PW1. Path: CE1-(AC2)-PE2-(DNI-PW)-PE1-(PW1)-PE3-(AC3)-CE2.
  • PW1 fails in the PSN: traffic moves to PW2 and AC1 stays active. PE1 connects AC1 to the DNI-PW and PE2 connects it to PW2.
  • PE1 fails: this is equivalent to AC, PW and DNI-PW failing. AC2 becomes active, traffic uses PW2, and PE2 connects AC2 directly to PW2.
sections.eli5: If the near door is blocked, the hallway links you to the working door, and the far side never notices. Only if the whole house fails do you use the spare route.

sections.title: Two-Side Dual-Homing
sections.content:
In the two-side scenario both CEs are dual-homed: CE1 to PE1 and PE2, CE2 to PE3 and PE4. Service PW1 (working) runs between PE1 and PE3, PW2 (protection) between PE2 and PE4, and a DNI-PW joins each dual-homing pair. The roles can be set by configuration or by existing signaling.

An AC failure, a PW failure or a PE failure is handled the same way as in the one-side case, with the forwarders on both sides reconnecting through the DNI-PWs as needed. For a PW1 failure the path becomes CE1-(AC1)-PE1-(DNI-PW1)-PE2-(PW2)-PE4-(DNI-PW2)-PE3-(AC3)-CE2. The RFC notes this scenario is mainly for services that need high availability, since it requires PE redundancy and network utilization.
sections.eli5: Now both ends have two doors and a hallway. Either end can reroute through its own hallway without bothering the other.

sections.title: Coordination Between the PEs
sections.content: The dual-homing PEs must synchronize the status of the AC, PW and DNI-PW and coordinate switchover. For PWs with a dynamic control plane, a protocol such as RFC 7275, possibly with extensions, can do this. For manually configured PWs without a control plane, a new mechanism is needed, for example over an embedded PW control channel. That mechanism is described in RFC 8185.
sections.eli5: The two door-keepers need to talk to each other so they agree who lets people in. This RFC says that talking is needed; another RFC says how.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The scenarios do not affect the security model of RFC 3985. The RFC points out that a disruption of a dual-homed AC, which is outside the core network, has less impact on traffic flows in the core and can avoid unnecessary congestion. The DNI-PW has the same security considerations as service PWs in the data plane, and the coordination mechanism is covered in RFC 8185. This document needs no IANA action.
sections.eli5: Adding the hallway does not make the house less safe, and a problem at one door matters less to the rest of the city.

layers.label: Attachment Circuit (AC)
layers.detail: Link to the customer edge node

layers.label: Forwarder
layers.detail: Switches payloads among the AC, service PW and DNI-PW

layers.label: DNI-PW
layers.detail: Joins the forwarders of the two dual-homing PEs
